chapters.1: An angel tells the elderly priest Zacharias that his wife Elizabeth will have a son, John, who will prepare the way for the Lord. The angel Gabriel then appears to a young virgin named Mary, announcing that she will miraculously conceive Jesus by the Holy Spirit, and Mary visits Elizabeth, where both women praise God in song. The chapter closes with John's birth and his father's prophetic words about the salvation God is bringing.
chapters.2: Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn, and an angel announces the good news to shepherds, who go and find him. Simeon and Anna, two devout elderly worshippers at the temple, recognize the infant Jesus as the promised Messiah when he is presented there. Years later, twelve-year-old Jesus stays behind in the Jerusalem temple, impressing teachers with his understanding before returning home with his parents.
chapters.3: John the Baptist preaches repentance in the wilderness, giving practical instructions to the crowds, tax collectors, and soldiers who ask what they should do. Jesus comes to John and is baptized, and a voice from heaven confirms him as God's beloved Son as the Holy Spirit descends on him. The chapter closes with a genealogy tracing Jesus' lineage all the way back to Adam.
chapters.4: Satan tempts Jesus in the wilderness for forty days, trying to get him to misuse his power, but Jesus answers each temptation with Scripture. Jesus then reads from Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue, announcing that he fulfills the prophecy of good news for the poor, but the hometown crowd turns hostile when he says prophets are often rejected by their own people. He moves on to Capernaum, where he casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others, and continues preaching throughout Galilee.
chapters.5: Jesus calls Simon Peter, James, and John to follow him after a miraculous catch of fish, telling them they will now 'catch people.' He heals a man with leprosy and later a paralyzed man lowered through a roof, forgiving his sins to the shock of religious leaders. He also calls the tax collector Levi (Matthew) to follow him and explains that he has come for sinners, not the self-righteous, using the images of new wine in new bottles.
chapters.6: Jesus defends his disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath and heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath, declaring that doing good is always lawful. After a night of prayer he appoints twelve apostles, then delivers a sermon of blessings and woes, teaching love for enemies, generosity, and not judging others. He closes by comparing a life built on his words to a house built on solid rock.
chapters.7: Jesus heals a Roman centurion's servant from a distance, praising the centurion's remarkable faith, and then raises a widow's only son from death in the town of Nain. When John the Baptist's disciples ask if Jesus is the Messiah, Jesus points to his miracles as proof and praises John as the greatest of prophets. At a dinner, a sinful woman washes Jesus' feet with her tears, and Jesus forgives her sins, teaching that she loved greatly because she had been forgiven greatly.
chapters.8: Jesus tells the parable of the sower, explaining how different people respond to God's word, and teaches that truth is meant to be revealed, not hidden. He calms a violent storm with a word, delivers a man possessed by many demons ('Legion') by sending them into a herd of pigs, heals a woman who had bled for twelve years simply through her faith-filled touch, and raises Jairus's young daughter from death.
chapters.9: Jesus sends out the twelve disciples to preach and heal, then feeds five thousand people with five loaves and two fish. Peter declares Jesus to be the Christ, and Jesus is transfigured in glory on a mountain before Peter, James, and John while speaking with Moses and Elijah. He heals a boy with a violent spirit the disciples couldn't help, teaches about true greatness and total commitment to following him, and sets his course firmly toward Jerusalem.
chapters.10: Jesus sends out seventy-two disciples in pairs to prepare towns for his message, and they return rejoicing over the authority they had over evil spirits. He tells the parable of the Good Samaritan to answer the question 'who is my neighbor,' showing that mercy, not mere religious status, defines true neighborliness. The chapter ends with Jesus gently correcting Martha for being anxious about hosting while her sister Mary sits and listens to him.
chapters.11: Jesus teaches his disciples the Lord's Prayer and encourages persistent, confident prayer to a generous Father. He defends his authority to cast out demons against accusations that he works by Satan's power, and warns that an evil generation will be judged for rejecting him despite seeing greater signs than Jonah or Solomon offered. He sharply criticizes the Pharisees and religious lawyers for their hypocrisy, obsession with appearances, and failure to truly know God.
chapters.12: Jesus warns against hypocrisy and fear of persecution, urging his followers to fear God rather than people and trusting that they are deeply valued by him. He tells the parable of the rich fool who stores up wealth but ignores his soul, and teaches against anxiety over material needs, urging instead a focus on God's kingdom. He calls his followers to readiness for his return and warns that his message will bring division as well as peace, urging people to read the spiritual signs of the times.
chapters.13: Jesus warns that calamity is not necessarily a sign of greater sin, and urges repentance using the parable of a barren fig tree given one more chance to bear fruit. He heals a woman bent over for eighteen years on the Sabbath, defending the act against religious objections, and uses the mustard seed and yeast to describe the quiet, growing nature of God's kingdom. He warns that many who assume they'll be saved will be shut out, and laments over Jerusalem's unwillingness to receive him.
chapters.14: Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath and teaches about humility, telling guests at a dinner to take the lowest seat rather than seek honor. He tells the parable of the great banquet, where those originally invited make excuses and the host instead invites the poor and outcast. He also teaches that following him requires total commitment, comparing it to carefully counting the cost before building a tower or going to war.
chapters.15: Responding to criticism for associating with sinners, Jesus tells three parables about things that were lost and found: a lost sheep, a lost coin, and a lost ('prodigal') son. Each illustrates how much joy there is in heaven when someone who was lost returns, climaxing in the father's joyful welcome of his wayward son despite the older brother's resentment.
chapters.16: Jesus tells the parable of a dishonest manager who is praised for his shrewdness, teaching that his followers should use worldly resources wisely for eternal purposes, since no one can serve both God and money. He then tells the story of the rich man and Lazarus, showing a reversal of fortunes after death and warning that people who ignore Scripture's warnings in this life won't be persuaded even by a miracle.
chapters.17: Jesus warns against causing others to stumble and teaches about forgiveness and the power of even small faith. He heals ten men with leprosy, but only one, a Samaritan, returns to thank him, prompting Jesus to highlight the rarity of real gratitude. He then describes the sudden, unmistakable coming of the Son of Man, warning people not to be caught unprepared like those in the days of Noah and Lot.
chapters.18: Jesus tells the parable of a persistent widow and an unjust judge to teach about persevering in prayer, and the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector to show that humility, not self-righteousness, is what God honors. He blesses little children as models of the kingdom, and tells a wealthy ruler to give up his riches to follow him, teaching how hard it is for the rich to enter God's kingdom. The chapter ends with Jesus healing a blind beggar near Jericho who calls out to him in faith.
chapters.19: Jesus calls the despised tax collector Zacchaeus down from a tree and brings salvation to his house after Zacchaeus repents and promises restitution. He tells the parable of the servants entrusted with money to teach about faithful stewardship while waiting for his return. He then rides into Jerusalem to shouts of praise, weeps over the city's coming judgment, and drives out the merchants defiling the temple.
chapters.20: Religious leaders challenge Jesus' authority, and he responds with the parable of the wicked tenants who kill the vineyard owner's son, a pointed warning about rejecting him. He skillfully answers trick questions about paying taxes to Caesar and about the resurrection, silencing his opponents, and warns the people about the hypocrisy and greed of the religious scribes.
chapters.21: Jesus praises a poor widow's small offering as more valuable than the wealthy's large gifts, then predicts the destruction of the Jerusalem temple. He describes signs of coming upheaval—wars, persecution, and cosmic disturbances—culminating in the Son of Man's visible return in glory. He urges his listeners to stay alert and ready, using the image of a fig tree's budding leaves as a sign to read the times.
chapters.22: Judas agrees to betray Jesus, and Jesus shares the Passover meal with his disciples, instituting what becomes known as the Lord's Supper with the bread and cup. He predicts Peter's denial and teaches the disciples about humble service rather than seeking greatness. After agonized prayer in the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus is betrayed by Judas, arrested, and interrogated by the religious council while Peter denies knowing him three times, just as predicted.
chapters.23: Jesus is brought before Pilate and then Herod, both of whom find no real fault in him, but the crowd demands his crucifixion over the release of the criminal Barabbas. Jesus is crucified between two criminals, forgives those who harm him, and promises paradise to a repentant criminal dying beside him. He dies with a final word of trust in God, and Joseph of Arimathea obtains his body for burial in a nearby tomb.
chapters.24: Women find Jesus' tomb empty and are told by angels that he has risen, though the disciples at first don't believe their report. The risen Jesus appears to two travelers on the road to Emmaus, explaining from Scripture how the Messiah had to suffer and rise, and then appears to the gathered disciples, showing them his wounds and eating with them to prove he is truly alive. He commissions them to preach his message to all nations before being taken up into heaven.
